title: Finland – Energy meters – Kaukolämpömittarit
description: Vantaan Energialla on kaukolämpöverkossaan n. 5 100 kpl lämpöenergiamittaria, näistä etäluenta on toteutettu noin 2 000 laitteen osalta 2G/3G- modeemeilla. Vantaan Energia vaihtaa tulevan 2G-alasajon seurauksena nämä 2 000 laitetta vuoden 2029 loppuun mennessä. Kilpailutukseen sisältyvistä lämpöenergiamittareista suurin osa on kokoluokkaa DN20-DN40 ja jakautuvat pääosin DN20 - DN100 kokoluokkaan. Yksittäisiä kohteita löytyy aina DN150 kokoon asti. Tämän hankinnan tavoitteena on saada Vantaan Energialle käyttöön uudet lämpöenergiamittarit, joiden vaatimukset, etäluennan toimivuus ja mittaustiedon saanti taataan pitkälle 2030 luvun puolelle. Kilpailutuksen kohteena olevien lämpöenergiamittareiden ja järjestelmä- /palveluvaatimukset löytyvät tarjouskyselystä.

title: Finland – Sewage, refuse, cleaning and environmental services – Jätehuolto- ja viemäröintipalvelut
description: Keski-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta jätehuolto- ja viemäröintipalveluista. Hankinta on jaettu seuraaviin osa-alueisiin: osa 1 Yhdyskuntajätteet osa 2 Tietoturvajätteet osa 3 Vaaralliset ja terveydenhuollon erityisjätteet osa 4 Loka- ja rasvanerotuskaivot Tarjouksen voi antaa yhdestä tai useammasta osa-alueesta, mutta osa-alueen sisällä on tarjottava jokaiseen kysyttyyn kohtaan. Jokaiseen osaan valitaan yksi Toimittaja. Tarjouspyynnön liitteissä ilmoitetut jätemäärät ja tarvittavien jäteastioiden määrät ovat arvioituja yhden (1) vuoden määriä. Hankittava palvelun ja kohteiden määrä voi vaihdella sopimuskaudella. Sopimus ei sisällä Tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta. Mikäli keräysastioiden tai kuljetuskertojen tarve muuttuu, yksikköhinnat pysyvät samoina. Hankintaan osallistuminen sisältää pakollisen tutustumistilaisuuden keskussairaalanmäen jätehuoltotiloihin. Ks. tarkemmin kohta Muut Asiat. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.

title: Sources Sought: Euclid Creek Fishway Construction - W912P425X11LG
description: Sources Sought: Euclid Creek Fishway Construction; W912P425X11LG SOURCES SOUGHT DESCRIPTION: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE, RELEASED PURSUANT TO FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) PART 10: MARKET RESEARCH. By way of this Market Survey/Sources Sought Notice, the USACE-Buffalo District intends to determine the extent of firms that are engaged in providing the services described hereunder for the Euclid Creek Fishway. This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes only and does not commit the government to any further contract actions, i.e., solicitation and/or contract. Respondents are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in responding to this Sources Sought Notice. Not responding to this Sources Sought Notice does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposals (if any) that may be issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. This is not a solicitation announcement; this is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This Notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP); it does not guarantee the future issue of an RFP; nor does it commit the government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, this Agency will not accept unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised that this Agency will not pay for any information or administrative cost incurred in response to this Notice; all costs associated with responding to this Notice will be solely at the responding party's expense. At this time, proprietary information is not being requested, and respondents shall refrain from providing proprietary information in response to this Notice. Responses to this Notice will not be returned. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this Notice does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this Notice. GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS: The purpose of this project is to construct a full width ramp with a series of 31 weirs and pools. These weirs are designed as an upstream-pointing arch with side slopes which concentrate the flow towards the center of the channel. Further design elements include a 4-foot-wide V-notch in the weir and 1.5-foot diameter boulders emplaced on the weir. The 31st weir (upstream most weir) will be constructed entirely of concrete the intent is to protect the less robust rock emplacements by breaking up incoming ice. Construction of the fishway will involve partial demolition and excavation of the spillway and underlying bedrock to anchor the fishway to the rock and replace the existing spillway. On the downstream end of the fishway the existing channel will be removed for a length of 150 feet. A four foot-wide embedded low-flow channel in the center of the fishway has been designed to provide sufficient depth of water and flow during normal low flow conditions to allow fish passage. A series of parallel transverse rock ridges that consist of 1�6� foot diameter stones will be evenly spaced along the length of the ramp to provide a series of pools and falls. This low-flow channel and rock ridges are designed to allow for the passage of fish and other aquatic life would occur. Contract duration is estimated at 10 months. The estimated cost range is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. REQUESTED INFORMATION: This Agency requests that interested contractors complete the following questions to assist the government in its efforts. 1. Provide firm�s name and BUSINESS SIZE, Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number) and CAGE Code, address, point of contact, phone number, and e-mail address. Contractors are REQUIRED to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) AT THE TIME ITS BID IS SUBMITTED to comply with the annual representations and certifications requirements (Reference: FAR 4.1102(a)). 2. In consideration of North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237990, with a small business size in dollars of $45.0M, which of the following small business categories is your business classified under, if any? Small Business, Service-Disabled, Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Woman-Owned Small Business, HUBZone Small Business, or 8(a) Small Business. 3. Describe the firm�s bonding capability. Is your firm capable of obtaining a performance and payment bond for a construction project valued between the project�s magnitude of costs? 4. Descriptions of Experience � Interested construction firms must provide no more than three (3) example projects with either greater than 95 percent completion or projects completed in the past five (5) years where the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages, and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. NOTE: Total submittal package shall be no longer than 5 pages. Please only include a narrative of the requested information. SUBMISSION OF RESPONSES: Respondents interested in providing a response to this Notice shall provide their submittals to Andrew Hewitt prior to 3:30 p.m. Eastern Time on October 22, 2024, via email to: andrew.b.hewitt@usace.army.mil with copy to Jeffrey G. Ernest at Jeffrey.G.Ernest@usace.army.mil. In all correspondence, reference W912P425X11LG and Euclid Fishway Construction. Electronic files (EMAIL) CANNOT EXCEED this Agency's size limit of 20MB (includes email and its attachment); files exceeding this size will be denied access to email inbox. NEGATIVE REPLIES ARE WELCOMED. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately from responses to this market survey.

title: Ground Ambulance Services at Ft. Polk, LA
description: The contractor shall provide Ground Ambulance Services at Fort Polk, LA in accordance with the Performance Work Statement included in the SF1449. All offerors shall provide the following items: Please complete the SF1449: Blocks 17 (to include the CAGE code and the Unique Entity ID Number) and 30 A - C. Please provide a statement that the offeror will hold its price firm for at least 90 days from the due date for receipt of proposals, subject to any changes that may occur as a result of discussions (if applicable). Please complete the provisions, as listed in the solicitation. Alternately, complete all provisionsin System for Award Management (SAM) and provide confirmation of completion and accuracywith offer. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM to be eligible for award. The SAM website is http://www.sam.gov. Proposals are due by no later than (NLT) 8:00 AM/CDT on 21 October 2026. Proposals shall be submitted via email to marc.a.flores3.civ@health.mil and salameya.paulouskaya2.civ@health.mil. Proposals received after the deadline will be considered untimely and will not be eligible for award. Questions are due by NLT 8:00 AM/CDT on 24 September 2026. All questions must be submitted in writing to marc.a.flores3.civ@health.mil and salameya.paulouskaya2.civ@health.mil. Electronic submissions with files larger than 20MB will need to be submitted in separate emails. All emails, regardless of the size, need to be received by the Government server, by the stated date and time. It is the offeror's responsibility to ensure the Government receives the entire proposal Factor 1. Technical: The technical proposal shall be addressed in sufficient written detail for the Government to determine if the Offeror understands the technical aspects of the Government's requirement. Offerors shall demonstrate how they will comply with the following subfactors: Subfactor 1: Technical Capabilities: - Offeror shall submit a detailed technical approach demonstrating its ability to perform all requirements of the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including the full range of ground ambulance services required under the contract. - Offeror shall provide management and operational plans, including safety procedures, staffing, training, quality control, and transition/start-up timelines from contract award through full operational capability. - Offeror shall provide a contingency plan addressing staffing shortages, vehicle breakdowns, severe weather, communications failures, emergency evacuations, and continuity of operations. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to respond to multiple simultaneous emergency dispatches, peak workload periods, and installation training events while maintaining required response times. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to provide and sustain the required staffing, vehicles, equipment, and operational resources necessary to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day, 365-day emergency medical services. - Offeror shall demonstrate its understanding of and ability to comply with all applicable Federal, State of Louisiana, Department of Defense, DHA, Army EMS, OSHA, HIPAA, and other regulatory requirements governing contract performance. Subfactor 2: Personnel Qualifications and Staffing - Offeror shall provide a staffing plan identifying labor categories, staffing levels, work schedules, and surge staffing capability necessary to meet all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall provide an organizational chart identifying key personnel, including the Program Manager, EMS Medical Director, Paramedics, and EMTs. - Offeror shall provide resumes for all key personnel demonstrating the education, certifications, licensure, qualifications, and experience required to perform the services outlined in the PWS. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to recruit, retain, and sustain qualified personnel while maintaining required staffing levels and minimizing vacancies to ensure uninterrupted mission support. Subfactor 3: Vehicle and Equipment Maintenance - Offeror shall provide a comprehensive vehicle and equipment maintenance plan demonstrating how ambulances and medical equipment will be inspected, cleaned, tested, and maintained in accordance with manufacturer recommendations and applicable regulatory requirements. - Offeror shall demonstrate its capability to maintain continuous operational readiness through preventive maintenance, equipment inspections, inventory control, and timely replacement or repair of vehicles and medical equipment. - Offeror shall provide procedures for documenting vehicle inspections, equipment maintenance, corrective actions, and quality assurance activities to ensure uninterrupted mission support. - Offeror shall demonstrate its ability to maintain operational capability during vehicle or equipment failures through contingency planning and resource management in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. Subfactor 4: Quality Management and Performance Assurance - Offeror shall provide a Quality Control Plan (QCP) demonstrating how contract performance will be monitored to ensure compliance with all Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements. - Offeror shall describe its quality management processes for identifying, documenting, correcting, and preventing recurring performance deficiencies throughout contract performance. - Offeror shall provide procedures for monitoring personnel qualifications, certifications, credentialing, mandatory training, and regulatory compliance to ensure continuous mission readiness. - Offeror shall provide a continuous quality improvement approach demonstrating how performance data, customer feedback, and operational trends will be used to improve service delivery and reduce performance risk. Factor 2. Past Performance: The Offeror shall submit with its proposal evidence of recent and relevant past performance under which YOUR company (the Offeror) provided the same or similar services in the public and/or private sector. Performance must have been by the Offeror (not by a subsidiary or sister company) either as the prime contractor or subcontractor. Offerors shall complete and provide the Project Summary Sheet (Attachment 1) on three (3) task orders or stand-alone contracts/purchase orders the Offeror will complete or has completed within the past three (3) years from the closing date of this solicitation that the Offeror considers most relevant in demonstrating YOUR company's (the Offeror's) ability to perform the proposed effort. Past Performance must be with the Department of the Army, other US Government departments or agencies, state and local governments and/or commercial/private sector clients. If the Offeror performed as a subcontractor on the reference project, the Project Summary Sheet shall explain what percentage and type of work that was performed by the Offeror as subcontractor. In the instance that an offeror submits more than three (3) Project Summary Sheets, only the first three (3) will be evaluated. Offerors shall use the attachment provided. Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQs) (Attachment 2) may be submitted (however not required) for each past performance reference identified on the project summary sheet (Attachment 1). Contractor Performance Assessment Reports (CPARs) will also be accepted. For projects that have CPARs, Offerors can submit CPARs with Project Summary Sheets in lieu of PPQs. Offerors shall ensure CPARs are finalized and reference the exact same projects detailed in the Project Summary Sheet. If a PPQ or CPARs was not received for any of the past performance references identified on the project summary sheet, the Government may conduct interviews to validate performance/quality information. A past performance reference will not be evaluated if it does not contain valid/current POC contact information, or if the POC provided cannot validate work identified on the project summary sheet. title: NX EQ Combi Oven
description: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Combi Oven product line as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as �national�) Requirements contract. Combi Ovens are thermally insulated chambers used in cooking for warming, cooking, and baking food, typically fueled by either natural gas or electricity. Food service ovens have thermostatic controls, which turn the oven on and off and select the temperature at which the oven will operate, and, usually, a timer. Food service ovens may have complex, computer-based controls allowing a wide variety of operating modes. They may be freestanding or countertop units. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to meet all requirements for the solicitation. The objective is to provide Combi Oven to be used by cooks within the VA medical centers and facilities, Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The period of performance is for a base of 12-months with four 12-month option periods. Please see the RFP and attachments for more information.

title: NX EQ Combi Oven
description: The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Non-Expendable Equipment National Program has identified the Combi Oven product line as a candidate for a VA-wide (otherwise referred to as �national�) Requirements contract. Combi Ovens are thermally insulated chambers used in cooking for warming, cooking, and baking food, typically fueled by either natural gas or electricity. Food service ovens have thermostatic controls, which turn the oven on and off and select the temperature at which the oven will operate, and, usually, a timer. Food service ovens may have complex, computer-based controls allowing a wide variety of operating modes. They may be freestanding or countertop units. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to meet all requirements for the solicitation. The objective is to provide Combi Oven to be used by cooks within the VA medical centers and facilities, Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). The period of performance is for a base of 12-months with four 12-month option periods. Please see the RFP and attachments for more information.

title: IRB Horizon TBIPS
description: The objective of this requirement is to provide professional services support to the Chief Innovation and Technology Office (CITO) to advance the modernization of the IRB’s case management and adjudicative support environment through the Horizons initiative. Under this umbrella, work may include a portfolio of related digital modernization projects intended to improve operational efficiency, service quality, sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability. This work includes initiatives to modernize legacy recording and information-handling capabilities through more current digital approaches; to streamline the creation, organization, and management of electronic case files through increased automation and standardization; and to support structured digital tools that guide and assist decision-making workflows in a more consistent and efficient manner. Collectively, these projects are intended to help the IRB assess, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that reduce manual effort, support more resilient operations, and strengthen the organization’s transition toward a more integrated digital environment.

title: APN - CETEMT New Facility and Compound, CFB Uplands
description: Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform the Design-Builder of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow the Design-Builder to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested Design-Builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project will include an Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.   Description of the Project and Services   This contract will provide the design and construction of the new facility and compound near the existing CETEMT (Counter Explosive Threat Equipment Management Team) compound at CFB Uplands. The new facility will be a single-storey building with an approximate footprint of 1,650 m2. It will include offices and workspaces, meeting rooms, maintenance garages and workshops, specialized spaces such as secure storage and a weapons vault, and support areas including a kitchenette, washrooms, and server rooms. The facility will be situated within a new exterior compound of approximately 6,500 m2, including parking areas.   The delivery method for this infrastructure will be a Modified Design-Build (MDB) contract. ROM estimate for the total value of the MDB contract is approximately $17M. It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.   Contract Number: 88076 Title: CETEMT New Facility and Compound Approximate Estimate: $ 17M Anticipated Posting: Q4 FY26/27 Description: Provide the Counter Explosive Threat Equipment Management Team (CETEMT) a new facility and compound on CFB Uplands in Ottawa, Ontario according to operational requirements.   Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a Design-Builder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated industrial security requirements of this project will be at FSC Secret. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing Design-Builders  early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, Design-Builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential Design-Builders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88076; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has  met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a proposal or a bid DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Priscille Vumi Leader, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada 343-596-6289 Priscille.Vumi@dcc-cdc.gc.caBidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. title: Subscription to metal and minerals economic data.
description: The Department of Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) has a requirement to provide senior management with detailed and accurate information on gold, silver, platinum group metals (PGMs), and other precious metals, including price forecasts; projections on supply and demand components; scenario outlooks for precious metals markets; detailed information about gold mine operations and gold markets; and other relevant information. NRCan will require access to a subscription to proprietary precious-metals market intelligence, historical data, forecasts, investment analysis, and gold mine cost data covering gold, silver, platinum, palladium, rhodium, and related precious-metals markets. The work will involve conducting thorough, data-driven research and sound economic analysis of the gold, silver, PGMs, and other precious metals markets and produce datasets, reports, briefing notes, presentations, and other materials that will help inform policy decisions. NRCan will also require user support as needed for questions surrounding the data, the web-based platform, and plug-ins and other online tools if available within three (3) business days.

Public Works & Government Services Canada (PWGSC) requires the services of an architectural firm (Consultant), acting as the Prime Consultant with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the delivery of services required for this project. The facility will be located at the Invuik Satellite Station Facility located in Inuvik, Northwest Territories. The Inuvik Satellite Station Facility (ISSF) is an international, multi-use science and technology facility and is located approximately 200km north of the Arctic Circle. NRCan requires the consultant to investigate options of accommodating their program in a modular building vs typical northern construction. A Class C cost estimate and conceptual schematic options developed through this study to seek early project approval to determine the project’s future viability. NRCan requires Pre-design/ Functional Programming and Schematic services to support preliminary costing and design work for a new multi-use modular facility of approximately 1,277m², excluding supporting areas to be proposed by the Prime Consultant and team. For this project, scope is limited to NRCan program requirements only, with future stakeholder participation or expansion to be considered separately once confirmed. Project stakeholder requirements are outlined within the Terms of Reference. See the Terms of Reference for more details.

title: DE01--ECO Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Consolidated Effort - RFI (VA-27-00011677)
description: Request for Information Synopsis Enterprise Service Desk: Integrated Service Delivery Model with Independent Billing and Outcome Oversight 1.0 RFI Synopsis Narrative Background and Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), Enterprise Command Operations (ECO) is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research supporting a planned future acquisition strategy for Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) support and its associated Contact Center Infrastructure (CCI). VA currently operates ESD Tier 0/1 support and CCI as two separate prime contracts under a Multi-Vendor Service Provider (MVSP) model, where the CCI vendor produces independent Service Level Agreement (SLA) compliance reporting and conducts formal quality assurance oversight of the Tier 1 vendor's performance. VA is exploring whether and how Tier 1 agent services and CCI platform management could be brought together under an integrated service delivery model, while determining what functions, if any, should remain organizationally independent from the delivery contractor to preserve objective performance, quality, and billing oversight. VA has not determined the appropriate scope or structure of any such independent function and is seeking industry input on whether independence is necessary, which functions require it, and the most effective means of providing it. The primary purpose of this RFI is to hear from industry on how an integrated delivery model would work in practice, i.e., how it would be structured, transitioned, and operated and to use that input, together with the Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimates requested below, to inform the resulting Performance Work Statement (PWS) and VA's decisions on scope, sequencing, and commercial structure. VA recognizes that consolidation may not be the right answer in every respect, and industry input that identifies where a combined model would be impractical, along with the reasoning behind that view, is just as valuable to VA as input on how to make consolidation work. This RFI is not a solicitation and does not commit VA to a particular acquisition approach. One specific issue on which VA would welcome industry input, particularly in the context of a combined model, is how outcomes should be classified if VA adopts outcome-based, automation-linked, or gainshare pricing. Under those pricing structures, the classification of individual contacts (e.g., AI-resolved vs. human-handled, genuinely deflected vs. merely relabeled, successfully automated vs. escalated) becomes the basis for what VA pays. If agent services and CCI are combined, VA wants to understand how a vendor would ensure that the entity performing the work and the entity classifying/reporting the outcome of that work don't create a structural incentive to classify ambiguous or borderline contacts in whichever direction favors billing. VA recognizes that transparent data feeds alone may not fully resolve this on their own, since the vendor typically controls the metadata structure, the correlation logic between systems, and the judgment calls in ambiguous cases. This lines up with feedback VA has already received from industry: multiple respondents to prior VA market research independently flagged the "AI-attempted-then-escalated" correlation and the "resolving tier" determination as fields that are self-reported, consequential to billing, and not easily produced by either vendor alone under the current structure. Given that feedback, VA wants industry's perspective on whether some form of independent validation of billing-relevant outcomes would be useful under a combined model, and if so, how narrowly or broadly it should be scoped. For example, whether it should focus solely on billing/outcome validation, or whether it makes more sense operationally to fold in general quality assurance scoring and day-to-day SLA compliance reporting as well. VA has not settled this question and is not assuming an independent function is necessary at all; VA's own data feeds, combined with automated QA tooling already in production, may prove sufficient on their own. This RFI invites industry input to help VA define the scope of the issue without presupposing a particular outcome. Strategic Direction VA's objective is not simply to combine two existing statements of work. It is to move the ESD operating model from a labor- and channel-centric structure to one organized around demand elimination, unified customer experience, and outcome-based accountability. Specifically, VA is seeking industry's perspective on an operating model that: Eliminates demand rather than optimizing contact handling. The strategic objective is not reducing cost per contact but reducing the volume of contacts that require human involvement in the first place, through AI-assisted self-service, proactive communication, automated fulfillment, and FboNotice-cause elimination. Presents a unified, channel-agnostic experience to the End User. The distinction between phone, chat, portal, and other channels should be invisible to the employee; the service environment, not the caller, determines whether AI, automation, knowledge, or a human agent is the appropriate resolution path. Treats AI and automation as the operating model, not an add-on. The relevant question is which categories of work should never require a human, and how the contractor is held contractually accountable for progressively moving categories of work off human agents. Realigns commercial incentives from resources consumed to outcomes achieved, while recognizing that outcome-based and gainshare pricing models raise the stakes on how outcomes are classified and who classifies them. Current Environment VA's current environment processes approximately 125,000 150,000 contacts per month across voice, chat, SMS, and self-service channels, supports roughly 600,000 End Users and 900 applications, and already has voice biometric verification, IVR-based automation (NICE Autopilot), and Medallia-based automated quality analytics in development or early production. VA's current CCI platform is NICE CXOne. VA is not presupposing that either of these existing tooling investments, the CCI platform or the automated QA platform, necessarily carries forward unchanged into a consolidated structure, and is asking industry to address both explicitly in the questions below. For purposes of responding to this RFI, the current functional baseline includes Tier 0/self-service and Tier 1 multi-channel end-user support, incident and service request intake, triage, resolution, and routing; knowledge management, process integration and new-service intake; workforce management, ACD/IVR and contact routing, contact recording and quality management, contact center platform administration; analytics and reporting; integration with VA's enterprise ITSM environment, customer experience capabilities, identity verification, existing voice AI/IVR automation and evolving enterprise self-service and AI capabilities; transition services; and continual service improvement. VA is interested in industry's perspective on evolving these capabilities toward an omnichannel service model and expanded AI-enabled automation. This description is intended to provide industry with sufficient context regarding the current functional baseline and potential scope under consideration. VA has not determined that all functions identified above will be included within a single future acquisition, nor has VA determined the final allocation of responsibilities among the delivery contractor, VA, other enterprise service providers, or any independent oversight function. Industry is specifically encouraged to identify functions that would benefit from common contractual accountability, as well as functions that should remain separate and the rationale for doing so. description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Lakehurst intends to negotiate and make an award on a sole-source basis with D-2 Incorporated, CAGE: 4EKX8 for a Fixed-Price contract. description: Der Auftrag umfasst die Werksinstandsetzung von Heizgerät des Systems SPz Marder. Die Bieter müssen im Rahmen der Angebotsabgabe berücksichtigen, dass die Angaben zu den jeweiligen Fachlosen lediglich aus den Vergangenheitswerten abgeleitete Schätzbedarfe sind sowie einen gegebenenfalls auftretenden Mehrbedarf (Sicherheitszuschlag) enthalten. Die tatsächlichen während der Vertragslaufzeit erfolgenden Beauftragungen können hinsichtlich der in einem Fachlos enthaltenen Bedarfsmengen der jeweiligen Versorgungsnummern abweichen. Die Obergrenze für den jeweiligen Auftrag bildet in jedem Fall die in dem betreffenden Fachlos zusammengefasste Gesamtmenge (Schätzbedarf + Sicherheitszuschlag). Eine Verpflichtung des AG, Einzelaufträge zu erteilen, wird durch diesen Vertrag nicht begründet. Die Vertragslaufzeit beginnt mit Zuschlagserteilung und endet nach 4 Jahren. Wenn der bestehende Vertrag zwischen der HIL GmbH und der Bundeswehr, egal aus welchem Rechtsgrund endet, kann die Rahmenvereinbarung durch ein Sonderkündigungsrecht beendet werden.

title: Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) en een gebiedsdekkend (Pré) Soortenmanagementplan (SMP)
description: Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. Gemeente Beekdaelen beoogt met deze aanbestedingsprocedure een gebiedsdekkend soortenmanagementplan (SMP), een pré-SMP en de uitvoering van natuurvriendelijk isoleren (NVI) te verwerven, inclusief begeleiding van de bijbehorende aanvragen omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag. De opdracht bestaat uit één overeenkomst voor de ontwikkeling van drie onderdelen. 1. Het uitvoeren van de opdracht Natuurvriendelijk isoleren voor gemeente Beekdaelen; 2. Het ontwikkelen van een Pré-Soortenmangementplan, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een (tijdelijke) omgevingsvergunning voor een flora- en faunactiviteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor Gemeente Beekdaelen; 3. Het ontwikkelen van een gebiedsdekkend SMP, inclusief het verzorgen en begeleiden van de bijbehorende aanvraagprocedure voor een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning flora- en fauna-activiteit bij het bevoegd gezag en ondersteuning bij eventuele bezwaar- en beroepsprocedures voor de gemeente Beekdaelen. Beekdaelen telt ongeveer 35.903 inwoners met ongeveer 16.915 woningen. Hiervan zijn 72,8% koopwoningen. Gemeente Beekdaelen heeft een totale oppervlakte van 7.840 hectare en de gemiddelde dichtheid van de adressen is 508 adressen per km2. Het onderzoek richt zich op het bebouwde gebied. Dit bedraagt ongeveer 12.6 km². Het onderzoeksgebied dient als basis voor de prijsvorming. Het definitieve onderzoeksgebied zal in samenspraak met de Provincie Limburg moeten worden vastgesteld gedurende de eerste fase van de opdracht. Gemeente Beekdaelen wenst binnen drie jaar na opdrachtverstrekking het NVI te hebben voltooid en te beschikken over een goed werkend SMP, inclusief een gebiedsgerichte omgevingsvergunning.

title: J061--Sources Sought Emergency Switchgear Repairs 539
description: The Cincinnati Veterans Administration Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement to provide repairs to generator operation to address failed generators & associated paralleling switchgear. The intention of this Sources Sought is to obtain information only. Please do not send a proposal. Requested information: To aid acquisition planning, we re seeking capable and interested firms for the information requested. If your firm meets the criteria please send the point of contract (ronald.heidemann@va.gov) the following, via email: Firm s Name Socio-Economic Status Whether or not your company has a contract vehicle we can order against If your company believes there is an alternative NAICS code please provide this If your company has any questions please provide. Contract Title. Repair Emergency Power Phase 2 Background. The chosen contractor shall provide repairs to generator operation to address failed generators & associated paralleling switchgear at the Cincinnati VAMC. The fulfillment of the project will allow for testing & repairs/replacement of existing equipment as required to restore full emergency backup generator functionality at this facility. Additional repairs required were identified by ABB during the initial repair of paralleling switchgear and the report is on the last page. Scope. The scope of this contract is to provide recommended repairs for both of the generators at Building #1. This system is currently functioning with only one generator, leaving the facility vulnerable in the event of a power failure at this site. Key task is to restore full emergency backup power for the facility to facilitate repairs of the existing equipment. Key task is test emergency power system and verify it works as intended. Specific Tasks. Maintain emergency generator availability for the facility Maintain security of the generator/switchgear room during the entire project. Work on generators can only be performed on weekend with prior coordination with the VA. Work will need to be done on two separate weekends, one weekend per generator work. Provide required repairs for the associated paralleling switchgear system per diagnose reports from ABB which includes Saturday work. Work includes the following items as identified in the ABB repair report: Replace two damaged MFR13 and reverse power relay to new protective relay and all installation/testing for both generators. Programming changes required for these replacement relays to ensure proper system functionality. Door modification to support the installation and operation of the upgraded relays. Wiring modifications to accommodate the replaced relays. Changes to the existing ABB systems drawings for these replaced relays. The General Contractor (GC) must coordinate as needed with the VA COR for testing of the generator control panels. Two new control panels (one per generator) have been installed. One control panel has been tested and verified to function as intended. The control panel on the inoperable generator requires testing and verification to ensure proper functionality. GC must provide a load bank for testing of both Generator 1 and Generator 2 on this day. 125% of load bank required. GC/subcontractor for paralleling gear work must test paralleling both Generator 1 (1500kW, 3 PH, 4W, 480Y/277V) and Generator 2 (1500kW, 3 PH, 4W, 480Y/277V) and verify it works with the 125% load bank. GC and subcontractor for paralleling gear must change priority of generators to verify they come back online/and shed as designed. GC and subcontractor for paralleling gear must provide a complete testing of the emergency power system including both generators and paralleling switchgear after all repair work is completed and verify it works as intended. Performance Monitoring Contract supervision will be conducted by the Project Section of Engineering Service at the Cincinnati VA Medical Center. Inspection will be made throughout the project and delivery and installation. title: APN - REPLACEMENT OF AIRFIELD LIGHTING POWER CENTRE (ALPC)
description: Advance Procurement Notice REPLACEMENT OF AIRFIELD LIGHTING POWER CENTRE (ALPC) 4 WING COLD LAKE, ALBERTA (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 4 Wing Cold Lake, Alberta. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services 4 Wing Cold Lake, Alberta requires replacement of the existing Airfield Lighting Power Centre (ALPC) building with a new ALPC building. The project will improve the reliability and efficiency of electrical power supplied to the Airfield Lighting System and support continuous flying operations.  The new system will supply power to new LED airfield lighting systems planned for installation over a five-year period starting in 2027. The existing ALPC will continue to power the existing incandescent lighting system until those systems have been replaced with LED systems.  The Department of National Defence intends to retain a contractor for work including, but not necessarily limited to, the following:  Civil and site preparation work, including concrete pads, slabs and footings for the building and fuel tank; extension of airfield lighting circuits to the new location; and design and construction of the new ALPC facility, including equipment, controls and lighting-control software.  Removal of the existing approximately 63.7 m² ALPC building, including its foundation, fuel tank and power systems, after the new building and power systems have been installed and commissioned.  Supply and installation of a new, approximately 100 m², prefabricated steel ALPC building configured in two sections: an airfield regulator section and a generator section.  Precast concrete manholes, airfield series lighting cable, and concrete-encased direct-buried electrical services.  Associated airfield electrical work performed by journeyperson airfield electricians in accordance with CSA Z463-18.  It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: 88023  Title: Replacement of Airfield Lighting Power Centre (ALPC)  Approximate Estimate: $11,100,000  Anticipated Posting: Fall 2026  Description: Design and construction of a new ALPC facility and associated civil, electrical, airfield lighting, controls, generator, fuel system, commissioning and removal work at 4 Wing Cold Lake Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a bidder will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a bid for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential bidders with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88023; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation (Contract number listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and has submitted a bid DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).
